blocks.text: Harbour Place Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Harbour Place is not a harbour or riverfront pocket in the City sources: it is a slope house pocket north of Austin Avenue and Como Lake Avenue, around Baker Drive and King Albert Avenue, below Como Lake, and the City publishes no boundary for the multiple listing service sub-area name.
The two addressed anchors inside the pocket are Baker Drive Elementary at 885 Baker Drive and Blue Mountain Park at 975 King Albert Avenue, at the foot of Blue Mountain.
Como Lake Park, 700 Gatensbury Street, sits just north of the pocket, and TransLink's route 153 stop at Como Lake Avenue and Baker Drive marks the pocket's north edge.

blocks.text: Harbour Place Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses are the stock here, on the Baker Drive and King Albert Avenue slope streets; no City, School District No.

The one housing-form fact the City does state nearby is plan-level, not stock-level: on May 27, 2026 Council kept areas east of Blue Mountain Street out of the Southwest Corridors land-use changes, and areas no longer proposed for townhouses in that review remain Small-Scale Residential.

blocks.text: Harbour Place Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Austin Avenue is the rule-changing street on the south side: the Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments adopted May 27, 2026 update land use along Austin Avenue and add a neighbourhood commercial node near Austin Avenue and Blue Mountain Street as redevelopment occurs.

Como Lake Avenue is the second corridor street: it was one of the two Southwest Corridors in that review, the other being Austin Avenue, under the Transit-Oriented Areas Update driven by provincial housing legislation.

blocks.text: Harbour Place Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Blue Mountain Park, 975 King Albert Avenue, is the park the pocket sits around, at the foot of Blue Mountain, and its spray park shares the 975 King Albert Avenue address.

École Montgomery Middle, the middle school listed at 1900 Edgewood Avenue near this pocket, is itself a seismic replacement project: School District No. 43 states the building permit was approved and the project issued for tender in September 2026.

The Austin Heights sewer work south of the pocket is in its final phase in summer and fall 2026, installing a new sewer main on Casey Street between Brunette Avenue and Cartier Avenue over about two months, weather dependent.

blocks.text: Harbour Place Houses: development and new projects

items.t: Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments, Southwest Coquitlam including the Austin Avenue corridor on this pocket's south side, City of Coquitlam plan amendment, mixed medium-density housing, townhousing and local commercial: the City states the adopted concepts are expected to add approximately 2,300 additional homes across the review area and add a commercial node near Austin Avenue and Blue Mountain Street — STATUS: adopted May 27, 2026 after a public hearing that day, read 2026-11-03.

Austin Heights Sewer Upgrade, Casey Street between Brunette Avenue and Cartier Avenue, City of Coquitlam, sanitary sewer infrastructure: final phase installing a larger sewer main and new manholes, then restoration, to serve the increasing population in the area — STATUS: construction summer and fall 2026, about two months, read 2026-11-03.

blocks.text: Harbour Place Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: The Harbour Place-specific cost check is servicing, not the rate: the final-phase Austin Heights sewer upgrade on Casey Street is City capital work, and a buyer adding units on a Baker Drive lot should confirm sewer capacity and any connection charges with the City rather than assuming the corridor upgrade covers the lot.

Route 153, Coquitlam Central Station to Braid Station, is the pocket's route: it runs Poirier Street, Austin Avenue and Como Lake Avenue, with a stop at Como Lake Avenue and Baker Drive on the north side.

No SkyTrain station is located in Harbour Place; the Millennium Line Evergreen Extension, opened December 2, 2016, serves stations in neighbouring areas, reached from here by the Como Lake Avenue and Austin Avenue buses.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Harbour Place, Coquitlam
Harbour Place has a misleading name, and I always point that out. The everyday water here isn’t a harbour at all; it’s Como Lake, through Como Lake Park.
Harbour Place home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

7 houses sold in Harbour Place with a median price of $2,000,000, taking a median of 25 days to sell at 96.9% of the last list price; 14% sold above list. They had a median $637 per square foot, a median year built of 1961 and a median lot of 10,701 square feet.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Harbour Place?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 7 houses listed in Harbour Place. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Harbour Place a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in Harbour Place had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Harbour Place from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 3 houses sold in Harbour Place over those 5 months, out of 273 in all of Coquitlam.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Harbour Place?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.

faq.q: Is Harbour Place on the water?
faq.a: It is a slope neighbourhood north of Austin Avenue and Como Lake Avenue, around Baker Drive and King Albert Avenue, below Como Lake. The named water is Como Lake itself, in Como Lake Park at 700 Gatensbury Street just north of the houses, with a 1.2-kilometre Lakeside Loop trail, a fishing dock, wetlands and a lake the City states is stocked regularly in spring.

faq.q: Which elementary school is in the pocket?
faq.a: Baker Drive Elementary, kindergarten to Grade 5, at 885 Baker Drive, is the school physically inside Harbour Place. Catchment is by permanent home address, so confirm the exact house address in the School District No. 43 School Locator.

faq.q: Will the Austin Avenue plan changes rezone my house lot?
faq.a: Not automatically. Council adopted the Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments on May 27, 2026 after a May 27 public hearing, updating land use around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre stations and along Austin Avenue, and the City states all proposed land-use changes east of Blue Mountain Street were removed during engagement. A Baker Drive or King Albert Avenue lot's designation still has to be read lot by lot in the adopted plan maps, not assumed from the corridor headline.

faq.q: Is there a bus on the interior streets?
faq.a: No interior-street bus routing is published for Baker Drive or King Albert Avenue. TransLink routes 153, 156 and 157 all run Como Lake Avenue on the pocket's north side; route 153, Coquitlam Central Station to Braid Station, also runs Poirier Street and Austin Avenue and stops at Como Lake Avenue and Baker Drive. House buyers here should plan on walking to Como Lake Avenue, Austin Avenue or Poirier Street for a stop, based on the published routings.

faq.q: What did houses in Harbour Place sell for?
faq.a: 7 houses sold in Harbour Place between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $2,000,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Harbour Place?
faq.a: The median was 25 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 96.9% of the last list price (14% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
